title: Cartesian affinization square for an open inside a quasi-affine scheme
statement: Let $u:U\hookrightarrow V$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], where both $U$ and $V$ are quasi-affine, meaning isomorphic to quasi-compact open subschemes of affine schemes. Put $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ and $B=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, let $r:B\to A$ be restriction, and let $j_U:U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $j_V:V\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ be the canonical morphisms corresponding to the identity on sections [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The square with top arrow $j_U$, left arrow $\mathrm{id}_U$, right arrow $\operatorname{Spec}r$, and bottom arrow $j_V\circ u:U\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. Equivalently, the inverse-image open subscheme $(\operatorname{Spec}r)^{-1}(j_V(u(U)))$ is $j_U(U)$, and its morphism to the open subscheme $j_V(u(U))$ is identified with the identity of $U$ by $j_U$ and $j_V\circ u$.

proof.text: Apply lem-a1-quasi-affine-open-principal-comparison-cover to u. Retain commutativity, the cover of H = range(u ≫ j_V) by the distinguished opens D(g) contained in H, and, for each such g, the equality q⁻¹D(g) = D(r(g)) and affineness of U_{r(g)}. By lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding, U is qcqs and j_U is an open immersion; j_V and u ≫ j_V are open immersions as well.

Prove q⁻¹(H) = range(j_U) pointwise. If q(x) lies in H, choose a principal chart D(g) in H containing q(x). The chart equality puts x in D(r(g)). Apply lem-a1-affine-principal-affinization-isomorphism to U and r(g). Its restricted affinization map U_{r(g)} → D(r(g)) is an isomorphism, hence surjective; choose a preimage y of x. Compatibility of the restriction with the inclusions gives j_U(y) = x. Conversely, for x = j_U(y), commutativity gives q(x) = j_V(u(y)), so q(x) belongs to H.

Apply Mathlib IsOpenImmersion.isPullback to the identity of U, j_U, u ≫ j_V, and q, with the commutativity equality and the inverse-image equality of the preceding step. The criterion uses the unique lift into an open subscheme and monomorphism cancellation, hence gives the fibre-product universal property. Flip the resulting pullback square to obtain exactly the stated orientation.
